title: The Lutherans reject the division of grace into sufficient and efficacious
source_text: THESIS I. ILLI Confessionis Augustanae Theologi qui Lutherani appellantur, non admittunt vulgatam gratiae divisionem in sufficientem atque efficacem. Idque quoniam una eademque Dei gratia est quae in credentibus operatur, & ab incredulis repellitur. Adeoque, juxta ipsos, illa ipsa gratia quam aspernantur & conculcant increduli & impoenitentes, ex se & in se efficax est, nec debet tantum sufficiens dici opposite ad quandam gratiam efficacem.
pass_a_gloss: THESIS I. THOSE Theologians of the Augsburg Confession who are called Lutherans, do not admit the common division of grace into sufficient and efficacious. And that because one and the same grace of God it is which works in believers, & is repelled by unbelievers. And so, according to them, that very grace which the unbelieving & impenitent spurn & trample on, is of itself & in itself efficacious, nor ought it to be called merely sufficient as opposed to some efficacious grace.
pass_b_english: Thesis I. The theologians of the Augsburg Confession known as Lutherans reject the familiar division of grace into sufficient and efficacious. Their reason is that the grace of God at work in believers is one and the same as the grace that unbelievers drive away.

On their view, therefore, the very grace that the unbelieving and impenitent scorn and tread underfoot is efficacious of itself and in itself. It should not be called merely sufficient, as if set against some other grace that is efficacious.
